items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you see some of the better-known people that played, like Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey? [INTERVIEWEE] They all came to the Lyric Theater.

ctx.x: Yeah, all that goes with it. That was a big thing in those times, double-entendre. You’re supposed to read between the lines. If you don’t be too rash or too bombastic, people will accept it. They had burlesque shows that done nothing but that type of material. Every town had its burlesque show, every big town, other than the sanctimonious states that was strict on them kind of laws, but they got people in the world who wants to hear that type of material. They go out for a good time. They want to laugh at…
Did you see some of the better-known people that played, like Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey?
They all came to the Lyric Theater.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And Ma Rainey had a whole gang of diamonds in her tooth.

ctx.x: card. And he was on there, and it said, "Diamond Tooth Jimmy Arnkey(?)." And De Paris was telling me, talking about Jelly Roll, he said, "Yeah, Jelly Roll took Jimmy Arnkey's(?) old lady, Mabel." Mabel had a diamond in her tooth. And Ma Rainey had a whole gang of diamonds in her tooth.
